hypothesis.observedProblem: runAgentLoop directly coordinates capability-specific flags, tool admission, instruction composition, delegation counters, and dispatch branches, so the core model/tool loop is coupled to every optional capability.
hypothesis.suspectedCause: Episode capability policy and execution were added incrementally inside the loop rather than represented as one phase-scoped adapter, leaving setup and per-call authority checks interleaved with generic conversation handling.
hypothesis.proposedMutation: Introduce one loop-ext WorkerEpisodeCapabilities adapter that owns phase-scoped tool selection/admission, capability instructions, delegation quotas, and optional-tool execution; have loop.ts ask it to initialize, execute calls, record delegation results, and close resources while leaving the model/conversation and tracing semantics unchanged.
hypothesis.expectedBenefit: The core loop becomes capability-agnostic and future optional capabilities can be added behind one adapter, while preserving existing phase gates, tool authority, quotas, and outputs.
expectedRisks: A moved dispatch branch could subtly alter delegation accounting or error text.
Resource admission/close sequencing could regress if the adapter lifecycle is not exactly preserved.
The adapter interface may add indirection without reducing all existing imports in this bounded patch.
